A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the PDI inhibitor, bacitracin, enhances the apoptosis-inducing effects of two chemotherapeutic drugs, velcade and fenretinide, on melanoma cells.

we have identified a new target in cancer, the endoplasmatic reticulum (the cell organelle responsible for the folding of proteins) and that this target can be inhibited using the PDI inhibitor Bacitracin, which increases apoptosis in cancer cells.
the PDI inhibitor, bacitracin, can be used to increase apoptosis in response to fenretinide- or velcade-induced ER stress and that this effect is dependent on PDI activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibition of the protein-disulfide isomerase (PDI) activity in melanoma cells can increase their death in response to chemotherapeutic drugs that induce ER stress.
the protein disulfide oxidoreductase, PDI, can act to protect melanoma cells from the effects of chemotherapy and that this protective mechanism can be abrogated by inhibiting P4HB activity.

the development of small-molecule inhibitors that target the protein disulfide-isomerase family of proteins may be an effective approach for enhancing the efficacy and specificity of chemotherapeutic drugs.
